annotations.text:
The Windows app does what the dashboard cannot: hotkeys, startup order, limits, launching.

So the first screen is a control surface for those, not a second dashboard. No totals, no top-apps, no weekly trend — that is the dashboard's job.

One list, fixed columns — NOT groups.

Grouping by purpose only works if an app has exactly one. Figma here has a hotkey AND startup AND a limit. Columns hold every combination; a column costs nothing when nobody uses it, which is why Main shows no LIMIT column at all.

Two things only this app knows.

Hotkey usage: Steam 44, Valorant 2. A binding that isn't earning its keys is worth seeing.

And the 144 apps already tracked make far better add-candidates than scanning the Start menu.

Strips appear only when something is actually wrong. Both states here are already detected today and buried in Settings.

On a healthy machine this artboard looks exactly like Main.

Today a new user sees "Nothing to show yet" and no way forward.

The app is already tracking everything they use, so the first offer should be to add from that.

Open question: ordering.

This list is in your configured order, which is also the auto-launch order and is what ⌥↑↓ reorders. That reverses the 2.0.4 change that sorted by most-recently-used — but "RECENT" is no longer the heading, so nothing promises recency any more.
